entries.title: The Internet of Things really is things, not people
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2015 one billion wireless Internet of Things (IoT) devices will be shipped, up 60 percent from 2014, and leading to an installed base of 2.8 billion devices.
entries.subject: Internet of Things

entries.title: Drones: high-profile and niche
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2015, the active base of non-military drones costing $200 or more should exceed one million units for the first time.
entries.metric: active base of non-military drones costing $200+
entries.subject: Drones

entries.title: 3D printing is a revolution: just not the revolution you think
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts, in line with the industry consensus, that in 2015 nearly 220,000 3D printers will be sold worldwide, with a dollar value of $1.6 billion
entries.subject: 3D printing

entries.title: Click and collect booms in Europe
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that the number of click and collect locations in Europe will reach half a million in 2015, a twenty percent increase on the previous year.
entries.metric: click and collect locations in Europe
entries.subject: Click and collect retail

entries.title: Smartphone batteries: better but no breakthrough
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that the rechargeable, lithium ion (Li-Ion) battery technology used in all smartphones will improve only modestly in 2015.
entries.subject: Battery technology

entries.title: Nanosats take off, but they don't take over
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that by the end of 2015 over 500 nanosatellites (nanosats) will be in orbit.
entries.subject: Nanosatellites

entries.title: The re-enterprization of IT
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2015 the impetus for IT adoption will swing back to the enterprise market following a decade of consumer-led technological change.
entries.subject: Enterprise IT

entries.title: Short form video: a future, but not the future, of television
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2015 total time spent watching short-form (under 20 minutes' duration) video online will represent under three percent of all video watched on all screens.
entries.metric: short-form online video share of all video time
entries.subject: Short-form video

entries.title: The 'generation that won't spend' is spending a lot on media content
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that US and Canadian millennials will spend over $62 billion on media content in 2015.
entries.metric: US and Canadian millennial spend on media content
entries.subject: Millennial media spending

entries.title: Print is alive and well – at least for books
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that in 2015 print will represent more than 80 percent of all book sales in dollars worldwide.
entries.metric: print share of worldwide book sales (dollars)
entries.subject: Print books

entries.title: One billion smartphone upgrades
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that one billion smartphones will be purchased as upgrades for the first time in 2015, generating over $300 billion in sales.
entries.subject: Smartphone replacement cycle

entries.title: The connectivity chasms deepen: the growing gap in broadband speeds
entries.quote: We expect the global number of broadband homes to have grown by about two percent to 715 million by the end of 2015. Average broadband speed obtained in most markets should increase by between 15 and 25 percent.
entries.subject: Broadband speeds

entries.title: Contactless mobile payments (finally) gain momentum
entries.quote: Deloitte predicts that by end-2015, five percent of the base of 600-650 million near-field communication (NFC) equipped phones will be used at least once a month to make contactless in-store payments at retail outlets.
entries.metric: share of NFC phones used monthly for in-store payment
entries.subject: Mobile contactless payments

notes: 14th edition by count from 2002. Rank is the order in the report. Publication month from the January launch pattern; exact day not confirmed.
